body:
Scanner found nothing to trade today: zero arbitrage opportunities across the Kalshi and Polymarket gold books. That's a legitimate quiet-day result, not a gap in coverage — Kalshi's contracts settle against a specific spot print at a fixed time, while Polymarket's contracts pay out if XAUUSD merely touches a level anytime during the week or month. Those are different bets on different mechanics, so their prices don't need to line up dollar-for-dollar even when they reference the same gold price.

The price levels embedded in the quotes look consistent with where gold has actually been trading. Kalshi's Aug 31 above $4,331.99 contract sits near a coin-flip (yes bid/ask 0.52/0.57), and its year-end $4,400 or above contract is similarly balanced (0.53/0.54) — both roughly bracket spot. That matches independent reporting: gold held above $4,400 an ounce on Tuesday after advancing for two straight sessions, with markets no longer fully pricing in a year-end Fed rate hike, and Forbes had the price of gold as of 8:16 a.m. ET at $4,391.41 per ounce on August 18. On Polymarket, the week-of-Aug-17 touch low $4,300 contract trades around 27-48 cents while touch high $4,450 trades around 23-29 cents — a fairly even two-sided spread, which fits a market sitting in the low-$4,300s to mid-$4,400s with real chances of testing either side.

Zoomed out, this fits a year that's been anything but calm: gold hit an all-time high of approximately $5,589 an ounce on January 28, then fell more than 18% from that record, before turning in its best performance in months last week. Today's flat scanner result is best read as the two platforms agreeing, not disagreeing, on a market that's simply pausing near $4,300-4,400 rather than presenting any mispricing to exploit.
headline: No arbitrage in gold: Kalshi and Polymarket agree, don't diverge
